title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: dual graphs of stable marked curves. Vertices carry a genus g_α and marked points I_α, and the half-edges carry an involution σ. The strata of the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} are indexed by such graphs, and specialization/generization between strata corresponds to contracting edges.

The previous page, conditions (48), characterised when a generalized graph morphism G'→G comes from generization: S'→S surjective, B̃'→Ã bijective, connected fibres, additivity of marked points, and the genus formula g_α = Σ g'_β + h_1(G'(α)). A crossed-out stability condition was dropped.

This page (p. 20 of the notes) does the following.

(i) Definition. A generalized morphism of ordinary graphs f: G'→G is a 'morphisme de générisation' if it satisfies only the purely combinatorial condition 1) of (48). That condition is S'→S surjective, B̃'→Ã bijective, and every fibre G'(α) connected. Here 'generalized morphism' means half-edges of G' go either to half-edges of G or to identities (vertices). In effect arcs go to arrows of Π_1(G), the path category or groupoid of G. B̃' is the σ-stable set of half-edges of G' that map to genuine half-edges.

(ii) Claim. G and f are determined up to isomorphism by the pair (G', B'). Here B' ⊂ A' = Ã'/σ is a set of edges of G': the edges that are kept, while the complement is contracted.

(iii) Proof sketch. Let G'_• be the subgraph with all vertices S' and edges A'∖B', i.e. the arcs lying over identities of Π_1(G). G'_• is the disjoint union of the fibres G'(α). Surjectivity of S'→S plus connectedness (equivalently 0-connectedness) of the fibres makes the canonical map π_0(G'_•)→S bijective, giving (49) S ≅ π_0(G'_•). Moreover (50) Ã ≅ B̃', compatibly with the involutions σ_B̃' and σ_Ã.

The next page adds the incidence map Ã→S, induced from B̃'→S'→π_0(G'_•). It then states that G is the pushout of G' ← G'_• → π_0(G'_•) (a discrete graph) in the category of graphs with generalized morphisms. This is the universal property of edge contraction.

In modern terms: generization morphisms of dual graphs are exactly contractions of a set of edges. The target is the quotient graph G'/(A'∖B'), and the pair (G', subset of edges) parametrises them. This is standard in the description of the stratification of M̄_{g,n} and in the morphisms of the graph categories behind modular operads.
errors: No mathematical errors. The argument is correct and elementary.
Minor ambiguity: B̃'→Ã bijective is what makes (50) hold. Injectivity of S-level data is not needed, since S is recovered as π_0(G'_•).
The equivalence 'connexes ⇔ 0-connexes' is a tautological remark, presumably meaning non-empty and connected.

ideas.what: Generization (specialisation) morphism of dual graphs, defined as a generalized graph morphism with surjective vertex map, bijection on surviving half-edges and connected fibres
ideas.modern_name: edge-contraction morphism of stable graphs (morphisms in the Getzler–Kapranov / Kontsevich–Manin category of stable graphs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford (1969) and Knudsen (1983); formalised by Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Getzler–Kapranov (1998, modular operads), Borisov–Manin (2006, generalized graph morphisms)
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts to my knowledge; the Esquisse d'un programme mentions the stratification of M̄_{g,ν} 'à l'infini' only informally

ideas.what: A contraction is determined by (G', set B' of non-contracted edges): S ≅ π_0(G'_•), Ã ≅ B̃'
ideas.modern_name: quotient graph G'/E (contraction of an edge set); vertices = connected components of the contracted subgraph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in graph theory and the moduli-of-curves literature

ideas.what: Arcs of G'_• described as those lying over identities of Π_1(G), i.e. graph morphisms viewed as valued in the path category or fundamental groupoid
ideas.modern_name: generalized graph morphisms (edges to paths/identities); 'graph morphisms as functors between free categories'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Borisov–Manin 2006 for the operadic version; free category/groupoid on a graph is classical

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, presumably in the 1980s, a category of graphs with 'generalized morphisms' in which edge contraction is a pushout. This anticipates the graph categories underlying modular operads (Getzler–Kapranov) and Borisov–Manin's generalized graph morphisms. It is a historical priority note, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: On dit que f est un morphisme de générisation s'il satisfait la condition 1) de (48).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: the combinatorics is routine and well established in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorics of edge contraction in dual graphs of stable curves; the only point of interest is the early, categorical framing via generalized morphisms and a pushout.
